newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria oil marketers push share index higher.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria oil marketers push share index higher.

text.p: Rises in oil marketing company shares pushed the Nigerian stock exchange index higher on Wednesday as other key stocks fell, Nigerian Breweries among them.
The all-share index closed at 6,957.48 from 6,956.08 on Tuesday.
Unipetrol rose 50 kobo at 57.20 naira and became the market's dearest stock as closest rival Total finished unchanged at 56.80 naira.
National Oil was 30 kobo higher at 46.00 naira, African Petroleum gained 20 kobo to 44.30 naira, Texaco added 13 kobo to 33.03 naira and Agip closed 12 kobo higher at 22.62 naira.
Nigerian Breweries fell 10 kobo to 19.50 naira -- its first fall since recovering from a 10 months-long slide to November.
Dunlop fell 40 kobo to 8.60 naira and has dropped 11.6 percent in three days.
"Dunlop's warehouses are packed full of unsold goods," one trader said.
A run on Guaranty Trust Bank's shares persisted, forcing the price down 20 kobo to 11.50 naira.
Some traders said the bank was overrated at its listing in September, adding it was only adjusting to its realistic level.
Ashaka Cement lost 10 kobo to 17.00 naira and traders said they expected it to fall further.
